definitions.explanation: Describes something that is not difficult. Written as {易|やさ}しい. Similar to {簡単|かんたん}.
Describes a person who is kind-hearted, gentle, or tender. Written as {優|やさ}しい.

examples.japanese: この{問題|もんだい}は{易|やさ}しいです。
{易|やさ}しい{日本語|にほんご}で{書|か}いてあります。
もっと{易|やさ}しい{問題|もんだい}をください。
examples.english: Please give me an easier problem.

examples.japanese: この{漢字|かんじ}は{易|やさ}しいから、すぐに{覚|おぼ}えられます。
examples.english: This kanji is easy, so you can memorize it quickly.

examples.japanese: この{本|ほん}は{易|やさ}しい{言葉|ことば}で{書|か}いてあるので、{子供|こども}でも{読|よ}める。とてもいい{本|ほん}です。
examples.english: This book is written in easy words, so even children can read it. It's a very good book.

examples.japanese: {彼|かれ}は{優|やさ}しい{人|ひと}です。
{彼女|かのじょ}は{誰|だれ}にでも{優|やさ}しい。
{優|やさ}しい{声|こえ}で{話|はな}してください。
examples.english: Please speak in a gentle voice.

examples.japanese: {先生|せんせい}は{優|やさ}しくて、{好|す}きです。
examples.english: The teacher is kind, so I like them.

examples.japanese: {祖母|そぼ}は{優|やさ}しい{人|ひと}でした。いつも{私|わたし}に{美味|おい}しいものを{作|つく}ってくれました。
examples.english: My grandmother was a kind person. She always made delicious food for me.

notes: This word has two distinct meanings with different kanji: {易|やさ}しい (easy) and {優|やさ}しい (kind/gentle). Context usually makes the meaning clear. When written in hiragana (やさしい), it could be either meaning.
